thread.title: Tech Today: Facebook’s Comeback, AT&T’s Quagmire, Ceridian’s Debut - Barron's

author: Tiernan Ray
title: Tech Today: Facebook’s Comeback, AT&T’s Quagmire, Ceridian’s Debut - Barron's
text:
Ceridian banner hangs over NYSE on its IPO day. By Tiernan Ray Updated April 26, 2018 12:33 p.m. ET Here are some things going on today in the world of tech :
New Tech IPOs Soar
The market welcomes a couple of tech IPOs today. One is nLight ( LASR ), a maker of semiconductor lasers for industrial applications. Its shares opened on Nasdaq at $23, above its $16 initial-public-offering price last night, and is now up $6.98, or 44%, at $22.98. More on the company in its S1 prospectus.
Another is Ceridian HCM Holding ( CDAY ), which started on the New York Stock Exchange at $28.90, above the $22 IPO price, and is now up $8.03, or 37%, at $30.03.
Ceridian is yet another offering in the “human capital management” market where Workday ( WDAY ) and others play. Its “Dayforce” application offers payroll and other employee functions. More in the S1 prospectus.
Facebook’s Comeback
Shares of Facebook ( FB ) are up $14.54, over 9%, at $174.23, after it beat Q1 revenue and profit expectations yesterday afternoon , and added $9 billion to its buyback authorization.
Lots of the sell-side today are using the snarky headline, “Senator, we run ads,” a reference to Facebook CEO Mark Zuckerberg ’s embarrassment of the out-of-touch Congress.
No ratings changes for the stock, that I can see, but price targets are going higher at most shops, into the $270 area at some places.
Credit Suisse ’s Stephen Ju , writing that the “sky is beginning to clear,” thinks that the “ comeback” is beginning for Facebook.
Ju cites ad revenue being “much better than expected,” and prices going up for those ads. Further, the looming GDPR privacy regulations in Europe will be "an unambiguous positive for operators such as Facebook,” rather than a risk. That’s because Facebook has "an everyday use case service offering which has a higher likelihood of receiving the consumer approval."
Among those less satisfied is Stifel ’s Scott Devitt , who keeps a Hold rating on the stock, while raising his target to $175 from $168. While there could be “near-term stability” for Facebook, “we remain cautious around longer-term user, engagement, and regulatory concerns,” he writes.
AMD Surges
Among other earnings from yesterday, Advanced Micro Devices ( AMD ) keeps adding to gains after its Q1 results beat and the company's outlook positively crushed expectations. The stock is up $1.30, or almost 14%, at $11.01, building on last night’s 9% gain.
The highlight last night was CFO Devinder Kumar raising the company’s outlook for the year. It now expects to have “mid-20%” revenue growth this year, up from an expectation offered back in January for “double-digit percentage growth.”
Among the bulls, Hans Mosesmann of Rosenblatt reiterates a Buy rating, and his $27 price target, writing that the company is “executing on all fronts.” He’s particularly delighted that AMD will be moving its server chip, “ Epyc ,” into a 7-nanometer manufacturing process later this year, getting a jump on Intel ( INTC ).
Sticking with a Market Perform rating, Bernstein ’s Stacy Rasgon musters the admission that "for the first time since this product cycle kicked off AMD may have given investors at least some reason to dream."
Intel Brings in the Big Gun
In AMD-related news, Jim Keller , a legendary silicon designer who put AMD back on the map with new chip designs, has left Tesla ( TSLA ), the company he jumped to after leaving AMD a couple years ago, and is now working at Intel.
Keller will serve as senior vice president leading Intel’s silicon engineering for Intel. Read more in Intel's press release .
Intel shares are up 97 cents, or 1.9%, at $52.35.
Qualcomm Tests Patience
Shares of Qualcomm ( QCOM ) are down 4 cents at $49.71, giving up last night’s small gains , after yesterday delivering fiscal Q2 revenue and profit that topped analysts’ expectations, but missed with its outlook for this quarter’s revenue.
CEO Steve Mollenkopf appeared on CNBC this morning to reiterate that he is “confident” in what he has told the Street regarding improved operating performance next year. He also said the company is in “active” dialogue with Apple ( AAPL ) about their legal dispute, which has wiped out hundreds of millions from Qualcomm’s royalties business.
Meantime, the outlook from even the bulls is rough. Chris Caso of Raymond James maintains an Outperform rating on the stock, writing that “while management has clearly frustrated investors, we're hesitant to sell at $50 since we think either NXP or a buyback should create a floor in the stock if not a catalyst." Qualcomm is in a pending deal to buy NXP Semiconductors ( NXPI ).
"But investor patience has clearly worn thin,” he concludes, and management has got to wrap up this legal stuff.
AT&T’s Quagmire
Shares of AT&T ( T ) are down $2.31, or almost 7%, at $32.90, after the company yesterday missed expectations for Q1 revenue, reporting $38 billion against the consensus estimate for $38.9 billion. Profit of 85 cents per share was three cents lower than expected.
The big negative was the drop of 188,000 subscribers to the DirecTV video business, worse than the 130,000 the Street was expecting. Offsetting that were gains of 312,000 in the Web-streaming version of the service, DirecTV Now . That comes with lower margins, however.
Jeffrey Kvaal of Instinet , who has a Buy rating on the shares, and a $43 price target, writes that there are “so many moving pieces."
A rash of 2018 accounting shifts and reclassifications make F1Q a riddle. We emerge from the quagmire with concern on margin pressure."
Andrew Bary ponders AT&T's 6% dividend yield in his piece this afternoon .
Samsung Eases Chip Fears
Samsung Electronics ( 005930KS ) stock rose 87,000 Korean Won, or almost 4%, to ₩2,607,000 in Seoul trading after it reported Q1 revenue overnight of ₩60.56 trillion, slightly more than the ₩60 trillion it had projected, but slightly less than the ₩60.74 the Street was estimating. Operating profit of ₩15.6 trillion came in higher than the Street's ₩15 trillion.
Point is, Samsung’s comments about memory chips are nice for the memory-chip companies such as Micron Technology ( MU ) and Western Digital ( WDC ).
Mizuho ’s Vijay Rakesh notes that “contrary to worries that Samsung would raise its DRAM bit growth outlook and swamp DRAM supply, Samsung focused on its target of 20% DRAM bit growth for 2018."
Also, "Samsung noted NAND tighter in 2H. In NAND while pricing is easing in 1H, Samsung noted demand drivers that could drive tighter NAND in 2H18."
Micron stock is up $2.07, or 4.4%, at $49.67, and Western shares today are up $1.21, or 1.4%, at $87.13.
